source.title: Can Multimodal Large Language Models Truly Perform Multimodal In-Context Learning?
source.authors: Shuo Chen; Zhen Han; Bailan He; Jian-Zhe Liu; Mark Buckley; Yao Qin; P. Torr; Volker Tresp; Jindong Gu

record.tranche_reason: The study investigates multimodal in-context learning, but does not test induction-head behaviour, its formation during training, token-index loss changes, or the relationship between those phenomena.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on multimodal ICL performance under changes to demonstration content and selection. These are related findings, but none measures the induction-head mechanism or the specific behaviours named by V1–V7. The paper cites In-context Learning and Induction Heads in its references; the cited results are not this study's results. Results for its proposed MMICES selection method are not extracted as induction-head evidence.
record.test_reason: The study measures multimodal ICL accuracy under demo-content ablations and selection strategies. It never identifies, ablates or tracks induction heads, previous-token heads, training dynamics or loss by token index. Olsson et al. is cited once, in passing, to support the idea that relevant demo context helps recall.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that multimodal ICL is driven mainly by demo text, and that demo images have minimal impact, attributed to masked cross-attention. Visual similarity still helps demo selection, which motivates MMICES (image pre-filter, then text rerank). MMICES outperforms random selection and RICES across most models and datasets.
record.recipe_differences: The study does not reproduce or apply an induction-head identification or intervention method; it evaluates multimodal demonstration content and selection.
record.method_sensitivity: Multimodal ICL performance changes with demonstration text content, presence of the query image, and demonstration selection strategy. Removing demonstration images has little reported effect, while removing the query image or corrupting demonstration text can have large effects.

fits_no_version.finding: Removing or blanking demo images barely changes M-ICL performance, while removing the query image causes large drops (up to 50% on VQA, near 100% on captioning).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In masked cross-attention MLLMs, query images matter far more to M-ICL than demo images.

fits_no_version.finding: Random questions significantly reduce performance, and random-word labels drive it to near zero. Different answers to the same question have only a marginal effect.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Multimodal ICL depends mainly on demo label space and text semantics, not on image-label correctness.

fits_no_version.finding: Masking demo visual embeddings leaves last hidden states about 90% similar to the standard setting. Removing query image embeddings makes them much more dissimilar.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Masked cross-attention limits the influence of demo images on the model's internal states.

fits_no_version.finding: RICES gains persist after removing demo images. Text-only retrieval underperforms RICES on OK-VQA and underperforms random selection on VQAv2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Image similarity is useful for demo selection because it retrieves query-relevant text, even though demo images contribute little in context.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Workshop/Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision
record.problems: The content-ablation results are described mainly qualitatively in the text and figures, without exact per-dataset values in the supplied text. The main content analysis uses Flamingo as an example; the text says similar conclusions are drawn from IDEFICS, with further results in supplementary material not included here.
record.rows_left_out: MMICES benchmark results and its per-model, per-dataset, per-shot scores are not extracted: they evaluate a proposed demonstration-selection method rather than induction-head behaviour or any of the specified version measures.

untested.parts: No circuit analysis of induction or previous-token heads; the only internal measures are hidden-state and attention-weight cosine similarity under image masking.
No training-time analysis; only pre-trained checkpoints are evaluated.
ICL is measured as task accuracy, with no attribution to induction heads and no token-index loss.
No search for induction-behaviour heads in MLLMs or other modalities.
Training data and setup are not varied for head formation; pretraining data is only speculated to limit M-ICL.
Text-versus-image demo ablations do not localise few-shot learning to any heads or mechanism.

record.verdict_notes: All rows are correctly linked to none. The content ablations are on Flamingo-family models (results in the text are for Flamingo; IDEFICS and Qwen-VL are said to behave similarly in the supplement). Excluding the MMICES benchmark tables is appropriate, since they show the study's own method.

versions.untested_parts: Whether induction heads compose with previous-token heads or implement the stated copying pattern.
Whether induction heads form abruptly during training, and whether that coincides with an ICL gain or a training-loss bump.
Whether induction heads carry most ICL, including the specified loss-falling-with-token-index behaviour.
Whether induction-behaviour heads occur across model families, sizes, training runs, architectures, or modalities.
Whether training data or training setup determines induction-head formation or persistence of ICL.
Whether other heads or mechanisms, rather than induction heads, mainly carry few-shot task learning.
Whether induction-head formation comprises multiple sub-steps or overlapping transitions.
